title: Split a string action into clap subcommands
summary: Replace a CLI that matches on an action string with a Subcommand enum, then let --db follow the subcommand with global = true.

turns.user: our todo cli takes the action as a string and matches on it. add happily accepts --id and the help is useless. want real subcommands

assistant.body: Let's move each subcommand's arguments into its own enum variant. Cli keeps a single field marked #[command(subcommand)], and a #[derive(Subcommand)] enum lists Add, List and Done. Passing --id to add is now a parse error, and each doc comment becomes that subcommand's line in --help. The match is exhaustive too, so the unknown action arm goes away. Note: the id for done is positional now instead of --id.

turns.user: nice. also let me pick the task file with --db, default todo.json

assistant.body: Add --db to Cli and pass the path into each function. An option on Cli is shared by every subcommand, so --db can go before or after the subcommand name.

turns.user: todo list --db x.json -> error: unexpected argument '--db' found

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. By default an option on Cli is only accepted before the subcommand name. Once clap sees list, everything after it is parsed as an argument of List, and List has no --db. Adding global = true to the #[arg] propagates it to every subcommand, so it lands in cli.db wherever it is written.
sed -i '' 's/#\[arg(long, default_value = "todo.json")\]/#[arg(long, global = true, default_value = "todo.json")]/' src/main.rs
